column3: “The sons of Uzzi” is rendered “the son of Uzzi,” and “chiefs” as “chief men.”
“The sons of Jediael” is rendered “the son of Jediael.”
“The sons of Aher” is rendered “the son of Aher.”
Close to the Hebrew; the Hebrew is abrupt.
The Hebrew is difficult (“took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim, and the name of his sister”); NASB renders “whose sister’s name was Maacah.”
“The sons of Ulam” is rendered “the son of Ulam,” and “descendants” as “sons.”
NASB makes “Ezer and Elead” the ones killed, with a relative clause; the Hebrew uses a new clause.
“In distress it was” is rendered “misfortune had come.”
NASB renders “Rephah his son and Resheph” as “Rephah was his son along with Resheph.”
The Hebrew spells the name “Non,” as NASB does.
“Daughters” is rendered “towns.” Many manuscripts read “Gaza” for “Ayyah.”
“On the hands of” is rendered “along the borders of.”
